title: Kitchen Literacy Project
about: The Kitchen Literacy Project teaches Syracuse teens to cook, free of charge. Jess Miller, a Syracuse University graduate, founded it in December 2023 with encouragement from Adam Sudmann of Salt City Market, and classes take place in the market’s teaching kitchen on South Salina Street.

Each week, teens from local after-school programs, including Hillside Children’s Center and Catholic Charities of Onondaga County, come in to learn the basics of cooking for themselves. The teen program is paid for by cooking classes open to the public, taught by local chefs, bakers and other food professionals on subjects from cake decorating to Ayurvedic cooking. Those class fees are what keep the teen classes free.

The goal is simple and lasting: young people leaving with kitchen skills and confidence they can use for life. Miller has also helped Syracuse’s branch libraries plan hands-on food programs, from fermenting sauerkraut to making borscht.
